items.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023
items.q: They’re thinking about Zeus and Atlas you know and [inaudible] and people like that and personas like that.

ctx.x: But anyway he would say, “Shalom [inaudible] and then Ishmael said, “Shalom Le Chiem” you know. The language got compromised you know, on both sides. But it’s really the same. Migrants, you know, the Arabic-speaking [inaudible] and the Jewish one was saying [inaudible]. I don’t want to get in an argument about that. That’s why I don’t stretch it, but to me if there is a God there can be no comparisons whatsoever. When they say we’ll reach out and touch the face of God — that’s symbolic you know. You know that’s…

Well thanks for sharing that. I’d like to — before we’re done here I want to just ask you about the last few years. It’s been interesting because some of your music from the 70s has been revisited and now they’re calling it classic, and at the same time you got hooked up with the two fellas from the Jazz Is Dead label and I just find it an interesting pairing.
